newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up on stable peso and Dow gains.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up on stable peso and Dow gains.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed up for the second day in a row on Friday as stability in the peso allowed the market to finally respond to a bullish Dow Jones.

"The market was firm although there was some profit-taking on same-day trades. Several things came together today, a more stable peso, the Dow rally and the fact that we broke through the 3,300-point barrier," said a trader at the Arka brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 31.17 points, or 0.95 percent, at 3,319.64.
Volume was moderate, but much improved on Thursday.
Some traders said the increase in volume was due to foreign buyers stepping back into the market to pick up cheap stocks.

"You can see by the volume that foreign investors stepped in as prices are still good, and they're moving ahead of an expected market take-off when the bulk of earnings reports are posted," said a dealer.

Autoparts maker Iasasa headed the percentage leaders after being hit very hard in September, gaining 3 centavos to 29 centavos (4 cents), followed by financial stock GFInver LCP and BCP series shares, which gained 11 centavos (1 cent) and 10 centavos (1 cent), respectively, to 1.11 pesos (14 cents) and 1.31 pesos (17 cents).
"(GFInver) reacted again to rumours of an alliance with Banco Santander," said a trader. "These have been around for a while, but they're getting very loud."

Gains by Mexican ADRs listed in New York helped shore up the IPC. Heavyweights like media group Televisa and phone company Telmex saw their ADRs gain 1-1/2 and 1/8 respectively, and their CPO and L series shares in Mexico gained 5.6 pesos (72 cents) and 6 centavos (1 cent) to close at 108.00 ($13.96) and 12.22 pesos ($1.58).
The broad market scoreboard meanwhile showed that a total of 107 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 53 to 34, with the remaining 20 unchanged.

One analyst said he felt that fundamental economic and corporate factors were good enough to allow the IPC to gather steam to try to break through the 3,400-point barrier, which it failed to do last week.

"We feel the market will settle down gradually and recognise economic fundamentals and (third quarter earnings) reports ... it may pause occasionally but climb towards a short-term objective at 3,410 points," said deputy research director Roberto Solano at the Estrategia Bursatil brokerage.
